shortIntro.title: 🪓 What You Need to Survive the Blocky World 🌍
shortIntro.para1: Minecraft is a sandbox universe full of blocks 🧱, creepers 💣, and endless creativity 🎨. To enjoy smooth crafting, building 🏰, and exploring without lagging into a glitchy mess, your device needs balanced specs and enough power.
shortIntro.para2: Low‑end devices can explore smaller worlds at about 20–30 FPS 🐢, while mid‑range and high‑end phones can handle epic builds and complex mechanics ⚙️ at silky‑smooth 60 FPS or more for the best experience. Creeper explosions 💥 have never looked this good.

faqIntroText: Common questions about Minecraft mobile performance — answered simply 🎤😄:

faqList.question: Can Minecraft run on 2GB RAM devices? 🤔
faqList.answer: Yes, but with lower graphics and settings. Larger worlds may lag unless settings are lowered.

faqList.question: Will Minecraft use 120 FPS on mobile? 🔄
faqList.answer: By default, Minecraft mobile often runs around 60 FPS, but some Android devices may unlock higher FPS depending on hardware and game options. Performance may vary.

faqList.question: Why does Minecraft lag in huge worlds? 🧠
faqList.answer: More loaded chunks, entities, and complex redstone increase CPU/GPU load — lowering render distance helps.
